candidates.name: hidradenocarcinoma
support_spans: Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement. Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm.
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of a slowly growing subcutaneous node with progressive infiltration of the overlying skin, along with the histopathological findings of tumor cells in an Indian file pattern, is consistent with hidradenocarcinoma.

candidates.name: apocrine gland carcinoma
support_spans: Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
candidates.why: The presence of GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association with tumor cells suggests apocrine gland carcinoma.

candidates.name: extramammary Paget's disease
support_spans: indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of an indolent, erythematous plaque in the axilla is consistent with extramammary Paget's disease.

candidates.name: mammary-like gland carcinoma
support_spans: Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies.
candidates.why: The immunohistochemical profile of the tumor, including positivity for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3, is consistent with mammary-like gland carcinoma.
